title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics + parity bumps (v1.92.0)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: unify SDK behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go for auth, retry semantics, and streaming ergonomics to reduce cognitive load for integrators and eliminate subtle parity bugs seen in recent customer reports (SUP-7421). This PR combines carrier commits: 1) standardize auth configuration surface (token providers + env fallback), 2) consolidate retry policy implementation and expose a concise RetryPolicy object/struct across languages, 3) stabilize streaming APIs with consistent connection/teardown semantics and backpressure handling, 4) several small parity fixes and TypeScript/Go ergonomics improvements, and 5) version bumps for all SDK packages to v1.92.0. Changes are intentionally backwards-compatible for the common codepaths; where defaults changed (retry backoff and max attempts), migration notes are provided. Testing: unit + integration tests added for all three SDKs and cross-language interop smoke tests run on CI. See ENG-2891 and ENG-3012 for design notes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + Linear link - [x] Python/TS/Go API signatures aligned - [x] Retry policy tests and chaos-injection runs - [x] Streaming teardown/backpressure e2e tests - [x] Updated docs and changelogs - [x] CI green and release-ready Notes for reviewers: keep an eye on the Python token provider fallthrough behavior (we added an explicit env provider before defaulting to system keychain) and on TypeScript streaming client helper names (we deprecated earlier helper in favor of a clearer API). Migration: minimal code changes for most users — a small opt-in config to adopt the stricter default retry behavior. Related PRs: internal parity fixes in redwood-sdk-python#413, redwood-sdk-typescript#527, redwood-sdk-go#210. Merge plan: squash-merge after CI passes and approvals.

release_notes: v1.92.0: SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) unify auth provider chains, introduce a common RetryPolicy API with improved defaults, stabilize streaming client ergonomics and connection teardown, parity bug fixes across languages, and minor performance improvements. Migration: adopt new RetryPolicy defaults by opt-in or set explicit config; see docs/sdk-migration.md for examples.
